title: Evaluation-isomorphism criterion for a dual pair in a closed monoidal category
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a monoidal category [def-sfb-monoidal-category] with specified internal Hom $H$ and adjunction bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes A,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,H(P,B))$, natural in all three variables. Let $P,D\in\mathcal C$ and $e:P\otimes D\to\mathbf1$ be given. For each $N\in\mathcal C$ let
$$\phi_N:D\otimes N\longrightarrow H(P,N)$$
be the transpose of $P\otimes(D\otimes N)\cong(P\otimes D)\otimes N\xrightarrow{e\otimes1_N}\mathbf1\otimes N\cong N$. Suppose every $\phi_N$ is an isomorphism. Let $u_P:\mathbf1\to H(P,P)$ be the transpose of the right unitor $P\otimes\mathbf1\cong P$, and put $c=\phi_P^{-1}u_P:\mathbf1\to D\otimes P$. Then the two triangle identities hold:
$$(e\otimes1_P)(1_P\otimes c)=1_P,\qquad(1_D\otimes e)(c\otimes1_D)=1_D,$$
with the canonical associators and unitors inserted. Thus these specified $e,c$ make $D$ a dual of $P$.

proof.text:
Write $T_{A,N}$ for the given transposition bijection, and write $E_N=\lambda_N\circ(e\otimes1_N)\circ\alpha_{P,D,N}^{-1}$, so $\phi_N=T_{D\otimes N,N}(E_N)$. Since $\phi_P\circ c=u_P$, naturality of $T$ in its source variable gives
$$T_{\mathbf1,P}\bigl(E_P\circ(1_P\otimes c)\bigr)=\phi_P\circ c=u_P=T_{\mathbf1,P}(\rho_P).$$
Injectivity gives $E_P\circ(1_P\otimes c)=\rho_P$. Precomposing with $\rho_P^{-1}$ proves $t:=\lambda_P\circ(e\otimes1_P)\circ\alpha_{P,D,P}^{-1}\circ(1_P\otimes c)\circ\rho_P^{-1}=1_P$. This uses only the supplied adjunction naturality and inverse identities; [def-sfb-monoidal-category] specifies the displayed associator and unitors.

proof.text:
Put $a=\phi_{\mathbf1}\circ\rho_D^{-1}:D\to H(P,\mathbf1)$. It is an isomorphism. Naturality of transposition gives $a=T_{D,\mathbf1}(E_{\mathbf1}\circ(1_P\otimes\rho_D^{-1}))=T_{D,\mathbf1}(e)$. For the last equality, substitute $E_{\mathbf1}$: naturality of the right unitor and the unit identities give
$$\lambda_{\mathbf1}\circ(e\otimes1_{\mathbf1})=e\circ\rho_{P\otimes D},\qquad
\rho_{P\otimes D}\circ\alpha_{P,D,\mathbf1}^{-1}=1_P\otimes\rho_D,$$
so the adjacent $\rho_D$ and $\rho_D^{-1}$ cancel. These are the unit identities obtained by naturality and the monoidal unit triangle of [def-sfb-monoidal-category] (in particular $\lambda_{\mathbf1}=\rho_{\mathbf1}$).

source.place: Tag 0FPU, example-dual-derived: fill in the omitted triangle verifications, abstracted from the derived category; monoidal constraints as in categories.tex, Tag 0FFK, definition-monoidal-category.

proof.text:
Let $g=\rho_D\circ(1_D\otimes e)\circ\alpha_{D,P,D}\circ(c\otimes1_D)\circ\lambda_D^{-1}:D\to D$. Expand this composite inside $e\circ(1_P\otimes g)$. Suppressing only the displayed associators and unitors, tensor bifunctoriality in [def-sfb-monoidal-category] gives the two contractions
$$e\circ\rho_{P\otimes D}\circ(1_{P\otimes D}\otimes e)=\lambda_{\mathbf1}\circ(e\otimes e)=e\circ\lambda_{P\otimes D}\circ(e\otimes1_{P\otimes D}).$$
Indeed both are the tensor of the two copies of $e$, followed by the common unit identification $\mathbf1\otimes\mathbf1\to\mathbf1$. Inserting $1_P\otimes c\otimes1_D$ before these equal composites, and using naturality of the associator and unitors, gives
$$e\circ(1_P\otimes g)=e\circ(t\otimes1_D)=e.$$
The last equality is Step 1. No tensor factors have been permuted: the two evaluations contract the disjoint consecutive pairs in $P\otimes D\otimes P\otimes D$.

source.place: Tag 0FPU, example-dual-derived: fill in the omitted triangle verifications, abstracted from the derived category; monoidal constraints as in categories.tex, Tag 0FFK, definition-monoidal-category.

proof.text:
By naturality of the given bijection in its source variable, Step 2 and Step 3 imply
$$a\circ g=T_{D,\mathbf1}\bigl(e\circ(1_P\otimes g)\bigr)=T_{D,\mathbf1}(e)=a.$$
Compose on the left with $a^{-1}$ to obtain $g=1_D$. Together with $t=1_P$ this is exactly the two requested triangle identities for the specified $e,c$; thus they form the asserted dual pair. Cancellation uses the two-sided inverse in [def-sfb-monoidal-category].

Stacks 0FPU (sites-cohomology.tex l.13149-13183, example-dual-derived) leaves out both triangle checks, so this split supplies them (D5). Step 1: injectivity of the transposition T applied to phi_P c = u_P gives E_P(1_P⊗c) = rho_P, which is the first triangle t = 1_P. Step 2: a = phi_1 rho_D^{-1} is an iso and equals T(e); this uses lambda_1 = rho_1 (Mathlib unitors_equal, CoherenceLemmas.lean:58) and rho_{P⊗D} alpha^{-1} = 1_P⊗rho_D (rightUnitor_tensor_hom, Category.lean:694), both under the cited Mathlib leaf def-sfb-monoidal-category. Step 3: interchange of the two disjoint evaluations gives e(1_P⊗g) = e(t⊗1_D) = e, with no braiding; I checked the strict computation and the coherence suppression is routine. Step 4: a g = T(e(1_P⊗g)) = a, so g = 1_D. The statement is correct and was not weakened. I tested it on Vect with e = r·mult (r≠0 gives c = r^{-1}; r = 0 fails the hypothesis), on zero objects, on finite-dimensional V with V*, and on infinite-dimensional V, where the hypothesis fails. The only citer, lem-fix-site-perfect-scalar-hom, uses the same c = phi_P^{-1}u_P and the same tensor order.
